title: Define layered revision identity across editor, scheduler, rig, and renderer
description:
## Summary
Five independently-verified artifacts answer the same question — "is this derived artifact still compatible with the source that produced it?" — with five unrelated mechanisms: an editor body fingerprint, a scheduler sequence number, a rig-cached pose skeleton reference, `SkeletonSnapshot.HasSameBoneOrder` structural equality, and an implicit "current definition" assumption. The 2026-09-12 audits call this out as one mechanism with one owner.

## Scope
- Define a layered identity: AuthoringRevision, GenerationRevision, SkeletonRevision, PresentationRevision.
- Every derived artifact records the minimum revision that invalidates it.
- Morphology/skeleton change invalidates a live pose binding (reject or rebuild) rather than silently reusing stale link lengths.
- Placement gestures pin the accepted preview revision at mouse-down and do not switch colliders mid-drag.
- Canonicalization records a version so cached or generated assets are distinguishable across semantic revisions.
- Generation signature = hash(effective config + canonical DNA + generator revision).
- Out of scope: the snapshot publish boundary itself (TSK-0095) and scheduler coalescing (TSK-0104); this task defines the identity those owners consume.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One documented identity model in the repo, naming each revision, what it covers, and what invalidates it.
- No derived artifact can be consumed without checking the revision it was produced from.
- A morphology edit during a live animation binding either rebuilds the binding or is rejected with a defined error; it never silently reuses stale segment data.
- A placement drag uses one immutable accepted-preview surface for its whole duration.
- A generated snapshot, a prepared mesh, and a placed preview each report the revision that produced them.
- Focused tests assert each invalidation rule; none rely on visual judgement.

## Validation
- EditMode/Runtime tests for: morphology-change invalidation of a binding; placement-revision pinning; canonicalization version round-trip.
- `Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` unaffected.
- Full-solution compile before the focused test run.

## Findings
- Verified: `SkeletonSnapshot.HasSameBoneOrder` compares IDs, parent index, source part, part type, mirror flag, position, rotation, segment state, endpoint, and child-attachment state — it is a rest-state compatibility predicate, not an order check. Its name understates the contract.
- Verified: `CreatureGenerationScheduler` uses only a monotonic `_latestSequence` for currency; there is no artifact revision.
- Verified: `SkeletonSnapshot.HasSameBoneOrder` is the only structural gate between rig and renderer bind.
- Audit provenance caveat: the 2026-09-12 suite was taken at branch bases that are NOT ancestors of the current HEAD `b5ba54b`. Re-verify each cited symbol before implementing.

## Blockers
- Sequence depends on TSK-0095 (publish boundary) so revisions have something to attach to; this task can define the model first and adopt it incrementally.

## Next Step
Write the identity model as an ADR-style note, name the four revisions, and map each existing fingerprint/sequence/equality check to one of them.

comments.body:
Audit synthesis 2026-09-12 (late) — external synthesis corroboration; independently re-verified against source.

SYN-05 (P1, 0.98) Confirmed: InfluenceWeightingPolicy identity is NOT carried by generated artifact identity.
- ResolvedCreatureSnapshot.ComputeRevisionId hashes only canonical DNA: CanonicalJsonWriter.Write(definition) then SHA-256 (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Definition/CreaturePartWorldTransformResolver.cs:212-221).
- InfluenceWeightingPolicy lives on CreatureGenerationConfig (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Generation/CreatureGenerationConfig.cs:20-51), external to the definition.
- GeneratedCreatureData carries definition + snapshot + mesh + colors + topology + skeleton + InfluenceDomain[] but no policy fingerprint (Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Generation/GeneratedCreatureData.cs:21-60).

SYN-06 (P1, 0.99) Confirmed: the runtime preview reads the live weighting policy during binding, so an already-generated artifact can be reinterpreted by mutable configuration.

This task owns the layered revision-identity correction. Acceptance gate: a generated artifact records the effective identity of every output-affecting setting read outside CreatureDefinition during binding, and binding never reads mutable generation configuration to reinterpret an already-generated artifact. Related owners: TSK-0224 (generation-owned final weights) and TSK-0248 (compiled-program context).
